2. The case of the prosecution is that the petitioners are said to have committed the offence under Sections 306 and 498A IPC.
Hence, the petitioners filed discharge petition stating that there was no offence made out.
Even as per the allegation made in the complaint, necessary ingredients of Section 306 IPC is not made out.
Further even in the chief-examination conducted by the trial Court, there was no material produced to proceed further.

3. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioners as well as the learned Government Advocate(Criminal side) and perused the records.
4.
At this stage, this Court is not inclined to go into the merits of the submissions of the learned counsel for the petitioner.

Hence, this Court is inclined to dispose this revision petition with the following direction:
(i) The learned Sessions Judge, Mahila Fast Track Court, Dindigul is directed to d i s p o s e o f t h e S . C . N o . 5 0 o f 2 0 2 2 w i t h i n a p e r i o d o f t w o m o n t h s

entities.text: Sessions Judge, Mahila Fast Track Court, Dindigul
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.

(ii) The trial Judge shall independently decide the issue on the basis of the evidence adduced by the prosecution without getting influenced by the order passed in the Cr.M.P.No.1112 of 2022 dated 20.03.2023.
5.
Accordingly, this Criminal Revision Case is disposed of.
Consequently, connected miscellaneous petitions are closed.
